lens: all three in turn: learning-scientist, examiner, learner-advocate

gates.G3: pass. No script available to the judge, so every next target was traced by hand in module.json (all S1-S6 branches, hints, sure_notes and END resolve)
gates.G4: pass. Buttons only; no typed input; no run-time model

reasons.R1: Probe before explanation almost everywhere (S1.start, S2.start, S3.film, S4.c1, S5.intus_case, S6.adh). Tell-blocks are limited to worked-case nodes reached on error (S4.w1, S4.w2) and recaps.
reasons.R2: Strong design: most wrong options carry 'Tempting / Why it fails / Right' feedback with claims and a sure_note branch. Pulled down by: S6 re-tests are the same stems as S3-S5, not another form; several distractors are mis-tagged or not a wrong model (see flaws); a few keys are findable by length (examiner lens).
reasons.R3: All twelve objectives are taught or tested on the main path. Fast lanes thin O3 (S2.a_ok skips why, sound and ileus probes), recovered only at S6.early and S6.silent. O2 is non-core and taught on S1 and S6.wall.
reasons.R4: Most nodes are one idea and one question and under 60 words per message. Pulled down by packed nodes (S1.recap, S3.inv2 three questions in one stem, S5.sites_case two questions, S3.sign_end recap), three-message feedback stacks (S2.a_x1, S2.a_x2, S4.c5_p) and the repeated 'Wrong model:' label.
reasons.R5: Fast lanes at S1.ok_both, S2.a_ok and S4.c1_ok. Hint ladder is hint, then Try again, then Show me why, and sure_note branches on confidence. Second explanations often use a different angle (S2.pain_hg vs S2.pain_h1).
reasons.R6: PYQ key vs current practice (TR1) is taught as two columns with a both-answers probe. Superlatives, which-is-NOT forms and setting qualifiers are drilled. Cold re-tests repeat exam items rather than drilling new vignettes.
reasons.R7: Decisions framed as clinical moments: dry adhesive patient on day 2, constant pain with tachycardia, 9-month-old, post-laparotomy hypokalaemia, stable caecal cancer.
reasons.R8: Direct and warm in the core nodes. Pulled down by a roughly 200-step path (sims: 117 to 202 steps), 'Yes.' openers on nearly every correct feedback, and an S6 that reads as a slog (every sim says so).
reasons.R9: Most wrong options name a model ('Wrong model: ...'). Pulled down by the S4 mis-tags (a distractor whose feedback corrects a different belief), the dominated catheter option, and S6 re-asks that do not diagnose retention. The four reports are judged in report_judgement.

segments.reason: Strong hook: PYQ stem committed before any explanation, tiered hints, and a both-columns probe that teaches the exam key against current practice. Flaw: after two misses on S1.virgin the path reaches S1.expl_virgin_adh, which says 'check the orifices' but never names the hernia, then drops to recap.

Predict-then-show for level, sound and strangulation. Feedback names the wrong model with 'Tempting / Why it fails / Right' and sure_note branches. Flaw: the fast lane at S2.a_ok skips the mechanism and sound probes that carry core objective O3.

Good trap work on films (S3.film, S3.num, S3.caecum, S3.coffee, S3.sign), but overloaded: S3.inv2 asks three test questions in one stem, S3.sign_end recaps what S3.sign_ok and S3.inv2_ok just said, and S3.film2 is a double negative (which feature is NOT seen).

Core management (drip and suck, override, 24/72 h timeline) is well built, and S4.c3 and S4.c4 teach the override well. Flaws: S4.c6 catheter option is not a wrong model and cannot win; S4.c8, S4.c10 and S4.c9 tag distractors to TR31 or TR23 while their feedback corrects a different belief; the key S4.c1 is the longest option.

Rich look-alike pairs with strong refutations: Richter vs Littre vs Maydl, child vs adult intussusception, sigmoid vs caecal volvulus, right vs left colon cancer. Flaws: S5.sig_case key is the longest option; 'Wrong model:' jargon in about a dozen nodes; S5.lbo_case and S5.sites_case are dense.

Cold check is not cold. Most items repeat an S3 to S5 stem and key in the same form, minutes later: S6.coffee (S3.coffee), S6.femoral (S5.femoral_case), S6.sig (S5.sig_case), S6.richter (S5.richter_case), S6.caecal (S5.caecal_case), S6.film (S3.film), S6.large (S5.lbo_case). The four sims cannot show retention. Only S6.pyq, S6.adh, S6.why, S6.timing and S6.paired are genuinely new, and some S6 hints are a generic line reused across traps.

best_parts: node S1.start, S1.both, S1.expl_same, S1.ok_both: the PYQ-key vs current-practice pair taught as two columns, with a both-answers re-test and a hint ladder. Graft as the model for every 'teach both' repair.

nodes S2.start -> S2.a_x1 -> S2.why_x1: predict-then-show for the level-dependent timeline; the feedback says Tempting, then Why it fails, then Right, with a sure_note for confident errors. Graft this pattern into S4 mis-tags.
nodes S5.intus_why_case and S5.intus_f: a mechanism probe after the age case (lead point, not the wall) that re-tests TR3 in a different form.
flaws: S6.coffee, S6.femoral, S6.sig, S6.richter, S6.caecal, S6.large, S6.film: same stems and keys as S3 and S5, asked again within minutes. Re-tests must be in another form (rubric R2, DP trap re-test). The sims count 35 to 60 repeats and a 117 to 202 step path. Replace with 8 to 10 new cases (new age, site, numbers) that cover TR1, TR22, TR23 and TR31 unaided.

S4.c6 (urinary catheter option, feedback 'part of the plan'): not a wrong model, so it is dominated and diagnoses nothing. S4.c8 (emergency laparotomy, colonoscopic decompression) tagged TR31 while the feedback corrects Ogilvie first-line treatment. S4.c10 (relaparotomy) tagged TR31 and S4.c10_p (NG drainage alone) tagged TR23 but corrected on the cause. S4.c9_p (drip and suck) tagged TR23 but corrected on the stone.

Telegraphing and labels: the key is the longest option in S4.c1, S5.sig_case, S6.sig, S6.film and S6.paired (DP1). 'Wrong model:' opens about a dozen feedback nodes (S5.virgin_f, S5.femoral_f, S5.richter_f_full, S5.child_f, S5.sig_f_discharge, S5.coffee_f_caecal, among others), which reads as a code word. S6.summary_t1's hint talks about strangulation screening, not the setting trap (TR1).
other_issues: S6.adh_t23, S6.adh_t22, S6.adh_t31 share one generic hint line ('Ask what the change in pain and pulse says'); S6.timing_t26a and t26b share one line too. Each hint should name its own wrong model.

The sims report claim IDs such as (K143) and (K27) inline in learner text. I found none in the say texts of module.json (claims sit in structured arrays), so the renderer may append them. Check render-report.
S5.theatre_h_pain: 'ask which finding is more than the usual presentation' is too vague to act on (novice sim).
merge_ideas: Keep the S1 two-column teach-both and the S2 predict-then-show structure, but replace S6 with a set of new-case items (new age, site, numbers), with a different form from the first exposure, for TR1, TR22, TR23 and TR31.
Graft the S4.c3 override language (the trial stops when constant pain, fever or guarding appear) into the S6 TR23 and TR22 hints, replacing the shared generic line.
Fix the S4 mis-tags so each distractor matches its trap, then give the catheter option a real wrong model (for example, 'wait for urine output before fluids') or drop it.
Shorten S6 to about 10 probes and end with the summary; the sims agree that a learner who has the traps in mind should not meet the same item three times.

novice.reason: Headline weak and the cards are specific and actionable (for example 'PYQs: hernia; today: adhesions'). Under-credits recovery: 19 traps show fell_open even though most were fixed on an in-node retry. Hints count 1 (only explicit hint taps). Calibration 'underconfident' is stated although the persona never tapped Sure; the report should say calibration is not measurable.

misconceived.reason: Names the wrong model for each trap, which is the diagnostic value a teacher needs. Overstates: all 20 traps are fell_recovered and the top line reads 'a solid base', although recovery came from one refutation and an immediate retest. Does not flag that the cold check repeated earlier items. 'You filled the grid wrongly' is vague.

strong.reason: Headline strong and the calibration verdict is right for a learner who always tapped Sure. Overstated: cold 42 of 42 counts repeats of items answered minutes before as retention. The text credits 'derived the cardinal features from the level' although the path only showed option choice. 'The way a good registrar reads a case' is ability praise.

guesser.reason: Two statements are false for this path: 'You used no hints' (the learner read every hint text after a miss, which the renderer does not count) and the fast-lane line 'answered a diagnostic correctly and confidently' (the first answer was wrong, and the confidence was not given). Render-report also crashes with KeyError 'choices' when the path ends at END.

notes: Learner-facing text was scored for teaching quality only. Factual content was not checked (knowledge-only mode). The sims were read as evidence of the path, not as the verdict. The module passes G3 and G4 on the hand trace, but a script run of factory.py validate would confirm the graph.
